challenges.name: estimates-vs-actual-quiz
challenges.title: Why the estimate was wrong
challenges.description: Two estimates from the CodeDev database: a new activity kind after a backfill, and a lesson progress query with two filters. Decide whether each statement is true or false.

questions.question:
A release added the activity kind 'certificate_issued' and backfilled 1,920,000 rows into activity_log (48,000,000 rows). The statistics were gathered before the backfill:

SELECT null_frac, n_distinct, most_common_vals, most_common_freqs
FROM pg_stats WHERE tablename = 'activity_log' AND attname = 'kind';

 null_frac | n_distinct
-----------+------------
         0 |         12

 most_common_vals:  {lesson_viewed,lesson_completed,quiz_submitted,signed_in,enrolled,course_viewed,quiz_passed,hint_opened,badge_earned,profile_updated}
 most_common_freqs: {0.41,0.22,0.18,0.11,0.03,0.018,0.012,0.005,0.005,0.004}

EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT user_id, created_at FROM activity_log WHERE kind = 'certificate_issued';

Bitmap Heap Scan on activity_log  (cost=1612.12..402170.40 rows=144000 width=16) (actual time=208.311..6120.877 rows=1920000 loops=1)
  Recheck Cond: (kind = 'certificate_issued'::text)
  ->  Bitmap Index Scan on activity_log_kind_idx  (cost=0.00..1576.12 rows=144000 width=0) (actual time=190.102..190.102 rows=1920000 loops=1)
        Index Cond: (kind = 'certificate_issued'::text)

Statement: "The estimate of 144,000 rows is 48,000,000 x (1 - 0.994) / (12 - 10): 'certificate_issued' is not in the MCV list, so it gets an equal share of the rows that the list does not cover."
questions.explanation: True. The ten MCV frequencies add up to 0.994 and null_frac is 0, so 0.006 of the rows have a value outside the list. n_distinct says there are 12 distinct values, 10 of them in the list, so the planner assumes the remaining 2 values share those rows equally: 0.006 / 2 = 0.003, and 0.003 x 48,000,000 = 144,000. The planner has no idea that one new value now covers 4% of the table, because the sample was taken before the backfill. The estimate is 13x too low; ANALYZE activity_log after the backfill puts 'certificate_issued' into the MCV list with a frequency near 0.04. The misconception is that the planner looks at the data when it plans; it only looks at the last statistics sample.

questions.question:
lesson_progress has 12,000,000 rows; lesson 701 is a lesson of course 7 only.

SELECT last_autoanalyze, n_mod_since_analyze
FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE relname = 'lesson_progress';

    last_autoanalyze    | n_mod_since_analyze
------------------------+---------------------
 2026-10-27 06:02:10+00 |                3120

Estimates for each filter on its own (EXPLAIN ANALYZE, first line):
  WHERE course_id = 7     ->  rows=240000 estimated, rows=239612 actual
  WHERE lesson_id = 701   ->  rows=10800 estimated,  rows=10812 actual

EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM lesson_progress WHERE course_id = 7 AND lesson_id = 701;

Index Scan using lesson_progress_lesson_id_idx on lesson_progress  (cost=0.43..10439.80 rows=216 width=32) (actual time=0.052..38.114 rows=10812 loops=1)
  Index Cond: (lesson_id = 701)
  Filter: (course_id = 7)

Statement: "The estimate of 216 rows is wrong because the statistics are stale; running ANALYZE lesson_progress will bring it close to 10,812."
questions.explanation: False. The statistics are fresh (analyzed this morning, 3,120 changes since) and each filter on its own is estimated almost exactly. 216 is 12,000,000 x 0.02 x 0.0009: the planner multiplies the two selectivities because it assumes the columns are independent. Here they are not - every row of lesson 701 is also a row of course 7 - so the second filter removes nothing, and another ANALYZE produces the same 216. The fix is to tell the planner about the dependency with CREATE STATISTICS lp_course_lesson (dependencies) ON course_id, lesson_id FROM lesson_progress followed by ANALYZE, or to drop the redundant course_id filter. The misconception is that every misestimate means stale statistics; check pg_stat_user_tables and the single-column estimates before you run ANALYZE and hope.

challenges.name: estimate-selectivity-from-pg-stats
challenges.title: Estimate selectivity from pg_stats
challenges.description:
After the trial import the CodeDev team wants a check in the deploy pipeline: given the pg_stats numbers of a table and the WHERE clause of a hot query, predict the planner's row estimate and whether it would use an index, so a misestimate shows up before the release instead of in production. Write estimate(case) with the planner's selectivity rules in this simplified form. The code runner has no PostgreSQL: this is plain Python over pg_stats-like JSON.

Input (stdin, one test case): {"table", "rows": table row count, "stats": {column: {"null_frac", "n_distinct", "most_common_vals", "most_common_freqs", "histogram_bounds"}}, "where": [{"column", "op", "value"}] (joined by AND), "indexes": [{"name", "columns"}]}. A list in stats can be null (count it as empty); a column missing from stats was never analyzed. Range predicates and histograms use numbers only.

Selectivity of one predicate (mcv / mcf = most_common_vals / most_common_freqs):
- nd = n_distinct when it is positive, otherwise -n_distinct x rows (a negative n_distinct is a fraction of the rows).
- rest = max(0, 1 - sum(mcf) - null_frac): the share of rows outside the MCV list and the NULLs.
- "=" v: the frequency of v when v is in mcv, otherwise rest / max(1, nd - len(mcv)).
- "IS NULL": null_frac.
- "<" v: sum of mcf whose value < v + rest x frac(v).  ">" v: sum of mcf whose value > v + rest x (1 - frac(v)).
- "BETWEEN" [lo, hi]: sum of mcf with lo <= value <= hi + rest x (frac(hi) - frac(lo)).
- frac(x) = share of the histogram below x. Bounds b0..bk form k buckets with the same number of rows: x <= b0 gives 0, x >= bk gives 1, otherwise, with i the last index where b_i <= x, frac = (i + (x - b_i) / (b_{i+1} - b_i)) / k. Without a histogram (null or fewer than 2 bounds), "<" and ">" use 0.5 instead of frac(v) and 1 - frac(v), and BETWEEN uses 0.005 instead of frac(hi) - frac(lo).
- Clamp every selectivity to [0, 1].
- A column without stats uses PostgreSQL's defaults: "=" 0.005, "<" and ">" 1/3, "BETWEEN" 0.005, "IS NULL" 0.005.
- Any other op prints {"error": "unsupported operator: <op>"}.

Output: {"selectivities": [one per predicate, in order, rounded to 6 decimals], "selectivity": product of all of them (predicates are assumed independent), rounded to 6 decimals, "rows": max(1, floor(product x rows + 0.5)), "plan": "Index Scan using <name>" or "Seq Scan"}.
Index choice: an index is usable when a predicate uses its first column; its selectivity is the product of the predicates on that column. Take the usable index with the lowest selectivity (the first one in the list on a tie). With no usable index, or when that selectivity is above 0.05, the plan is "Seq Scan" (simplified: the real crossover depends on costs and on how the rows are ordered on disk). Compute products and comparisons with unrounded values.

Example: enrollments with 20,000,000 rows, status MCVs {active 0.7, completed 0.2, cancelled 0.08, refunded 0.02}, course_id n_distinct 1840 with MCVs 7, 12, 3 (0.031, 0.024, 0.019). WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND course_id = 42 gives 0.08 and 0.926 / 1837 = 0.000504, rows 807, and the course_id index.
hints: status has the MCVs active 0.71, completed 0.21 and cancelled 0.08 and no NULLs. What share of the rows is left for every value that is not in the list, and what does that make the estimate for 'trial'?

Work through the rules in order for each predicate: first decide whether the column has stats at all, then compute nd and rest once, then branch on the operator. For ranges, the MCV part and the histogram part are added, and only the histogram part is scaled by rest. For the plan, look only at predicates on the first column of each index, and check how the threshold treats a selectivity of exactly 0.05.

A similar range on different numbers: score has null_frac 0.1, MCVs {100: 0.2}, histogram bounds [0, 20, 50, 60, 90] (4 buckets). rest = 1 - 0.2 - 0.1 = 0.7. For score < 55: no MCV is below 55; 55 lies in bucket 2 (50..60), so frac = (2 + 5 / 10) / 4 = 0.625 and the selectivity is 0.7 x 0.625 = 0.4375. For score > 55: 0.2 (the MCV 100) + 0.7 x 0.375 = 0.4625.

tests.name: MCV status and a course outside the MCV list: the course_id index wins
The incident: 'trial' is not in stale statistics, so the estimate is 1 row
After ANALYZE: 'trial' is 10.5% of the rows, above the threshold: Seq Scan
Negative n_distinct: user_id has 0.0125 x 48M distinct values
Ranges: BETWEEN and < with MCV and histogram parts, > without a histogram
No stats: defaults; IS NULL uses null_frac; a selectivity of exactly 0.05 still picks the index
Large stats: 1000 MCVs and 1001 histogram bounds on user_id
An operator the estimator does not support: an error
